word_for_word: वाचिकं तप आह -- अनुद्वेगेति। उद्वेगं भयं न करोतीत्यनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं? सत्यं च श्रोतुःप्रियं च हितं च परिणामे सुखकरम्? स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं वेदाभ्यासश्च वाङ्मयं वाचा निर्वर्त्यं तपः।

He states verbal austerity. Speech that causes no agitation or fear, is true, pleasing to the hearer, beneficial, and produces well-being in the end, together with recitation and practice of one’s Vedic study, is austerity of speech, performed by speech.

मानसं तप आह -- मनःप्रसाद इति। मनसः प्रसादः स्वस्थता? सौम्यत्वमक्रूरता? मौनं मुनेर्भावः। मननमित्यर्थः। आत्मनो मनसो विनिग्रहः विषयेभ्यः? प्रत्याहारः? भावसंशुद्धिर्व्यवहारे मायाराहित्यमित्येतन्मानसं तपः।

He states mental austerity. Serenity of mind is mental well-being; gentleness is absence of cruelty; silence is the state of a muni, meaning reflection; control of the self means withdrawal and restraint of the mind from sense objects; purity of disposition means absence of deceit in conduct. These constitute mental austerity.

तदेवं शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्निर्वर्त्यं त्रिविधं तपो दर्शितम्। त्रिविधस्यापि तपसः सात्त्विकादिभेदेन त्रैविध्यमाह -- श्रद्धयेति त्रिभिः। त्रिविधमपि तपः श्रेष्ठया श्रद्धया फलाकाङ्क्षाशून्यैर्युक्तैरेकाग्रचित्तैर्नरैस्तप्तं तत्सात्त्विकं कथयन्ति।

Thus the three kinds of austerity performed by body, speech and mind have been described. He now gives the threefold sattvic, rajasic and tamasic division applying to all three. The learned call all three forms sattvic when practiced by disciplined, concentrated persons with the highest faith and without desire for fruit.

राजसं तप आह -- सत्कार इति। सत्कारः साधुकारः साधुरयमिति तापस इत्यादि वाक्पूजा? मानः प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादनादिः दैहिकीपूजाऽर्थलाभादिः? एतदर्थं दम्भेन च यत्तपः क्रियते अतएव चलं अनियतं अध्रुवं च क्षणिकं। यदेवंभूतं तपस्तदिह राजसं प्रोक्तम्।

He states rajasic austerity. ‘Respect’ is verbal honor such as praise—‘he is a holy man, an ascetic’; ‘honor’ includes bodily acts such as rising and saluting and also gains such as wealth. Austerity practiced for these purposes and with hypocrisy is therefore unstable, irregular and impermanent, lasting only briefly. Austerity of this kind is called rajasic here.
तामसं तप आह -- मूढेति। मूढग्राहेणाविवेककृतेन दुराग्रहेणात्मनः पीडया यत्तपः क्रियते परस्योत्सादनार्थं वाऽन्यस्य विनाशार्थमभिचाररूपं तत्तामसमुदाहृतं कथितम्।

He states tamasic austerity. Austerity practiced through foolish obstinacy produced by lack of discrimination, with self-torment, or in the form of harmful rites intended to ruin or destroy another person, is declared tamasic.

पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञातमेव दानस्य त्रैविध्यमाह -- दातव्यमिति। दातव्यमित्येवं निश्चयेन यद्दानं दीयते? अनुपकारिणे,प्रत्युपकारासमर्थाय। देशे कुरुक्षेत्रादौ? काले ग्रहणादौ? पात्रे चेति देशकालादिसाहचर्यात्सप्तमी प्रयुक्ता। पात्रभूताय तपःश्रुतादिसंपन्नाय ब्राह्मणायेत्यर्थः। यद्वा पात्र इति चतुर्थ्येवैषा। पात्रे इति तृजन्तं। रक्षकायेत्यर्थः। स हि सर्वस्मादापद्गणाद्दातारं पातीति। यदेवंभूतं दानं तत्सात्त्विकम्।

He now gives the promised threefold division of charity. A gift given with the firm thought ‘it ought to be given,’ to one unable to make a return, in a proper place such as Kurukṣetra, at a proper time such as an eclipse, and to a worthy recipient—a Brāhmaṇa endowed with austerity, learning and the like—is sattvic. The locative ‘in recipient’ is used alongside place and time; alternatively it can be understood as a dative from a derivative meaning ‘protector,’ because such a worthy recipient protects the donor from every group of dangers.
राजसं दानमाह -- यत्त्विति। कालान्तरेऽयं मां प्रत्युपकारं करिष्यतीत्येवमर्थम्? फलं वा स्वर्गादिकमुद्दिश्य यत्पुनर्दानं दीयते परिक्लिष्टं चित्तक्लेशयुक्तं यथा भवत्येवंभूतं तद्दानं राजसमुदाहृतं कथितम्।
He states rajasic charity. A gift given with the aim ‘later this person will repay me,’ or with a fruit such as heaven in view, and given reluctantly with mental distress, is declared rajasic.

तामसं दानमाह -- अदेशेति। अदेशे अशुचिस्थाने? अकाले अशौचसमये? अपात्रेभ्यो विटनटनर्तकादिभ्यो यद्दानं दीयते। देशकालपात्रसंपत्तावपि असत्कृतं पादप्रक्षालनादिसत्कारशून्यम्? अवज्ञातं तिरस्कारयुक्तं। एंवभूतं दानं तामसमुदाहृतम्।

He states tamasic charity. A gift given in an improper, impure place, at an improper time such as a period of impurity, or to unworthy recipients such as certain entertainers and dancers; or even where place, time and recipient are proper, a gift given without respectful treatment such as washing the recipient’s feet and with contempt—is declared tamasic.

ननु चैवं विचार्यमाणे सर्वमपि यज्ञतपोदानादि राजसतामसप्रायमेवेति व्यर्थो यज्ञादिप्रयास इत्याशङ्क्य तथाविधस्यापि सात्त्विकत्वापादनप्रकारं दर्शयितुमाह -- ओमिति। ऊँतत्सदित्येवं त्रिविधो ब्रह्मणाः परमात्मनो निर्देशो नाम व्यपदेशः स्मृतः शिष्टैः। तत्र तावत्ओमिति त्रिवृद्ब्रह्म इत्यादिश्रुतिप्रसिद्धेरोमिति ब्रह्मणो नाम? जगत्कारणत्वेनातिप्रसिद्धत्वात्? अविदुषां परोक्षत्वाच्च। तच्छब्दोऽपि ब्रह्मणो नाम। परमार्थसत्त्वसाधुत्वप्रशस्तत्वाभिः सच्छब्दो ब्रह्मणो नामसदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीत् इत्यादिश्रुतेः। अयं त्रिविधोऽपि नामनिर्देशो विगुणमपि सगुणीकर्तुं समर्थ इत्याशयेन स्तौति। तेन त्रिविधेन ब्रह्मणो निर्देशेन ब्राह्मणाश्च वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च पूर्वं सृष्ट्यादौ विहिताः विधात्रा निर्मिताः सगुणीकृता वा। यद्वा यस्यायं त्रिविधो निर्देशस्तेन परमात्मना ब्राह्मणादयः पवित्रतमाः सृष्टाः। तस्मात्तस्यायं त्रिविधो निर्देशोऽतिप्रशस्त इत्यर्थः।

An objection arises: judged this strictly, sacrifice, austerity, charity and the rest would mostly be rajasic or tamasic, making the effort useless. Therefore He shows how even such practices can be rendered sattvic. ‘Oṃ Tat Sat’ is remembered by the learned as the threefold designation or name of Brahman, the Supreme Self. Oṃ is a name of Brahman, well known from scriptures such as ‘Oṃ is the threefold Brahman’; ‘Tat’ is also a name of Brahman because Brahman is supremely famous as the cause of the universe and is remote to the ignorant; ‘Sat’ is a name of Brahman because of ultimate reality, goodness and excellence, as in ‘Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning.’ He praises this threefold naming as capable of supplying excellence even where a rite has defects. By this threefold designation of Brahman, Brāhmaṇas, Vedas and sacrifices were ordained or rendered excellent by the Creator at the beginning of creation. Alternatively, the Supreme Self designated by these three names created the supremely pure Brāhmaṇas, Vedas and sacrifices. Therefore this threefold designation is exceedingly praiseworthy.

इदानीं प्रत्येकमोंकारादीनां प्राशस्त्यं दर्शयिष्यन्नोंकारस्य तदेवाह -- तस्मादिति। यस्मादेवं ब्रह्मणो निर्देशः प्रशस्तस्तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य उच्चार्य कृता वेदवादीनां यज्ञाद्याः शास्त्रोक्ताः क्रियाः सततं सर्वदा अङ्गवैकल्येऽपि प्रकर्षेण वर्तन्ते। सगुणा भवन्तीत्यर्थः।

Now, intending to show separately the excellence of Oṃ and the other names, He first explains Oṃ. Because this designation of Brahman is so praiseworthy, scripturally prescribed rites such as sacrifices performed by followers of the Veda after uttering Oṃ remain effective and become endowed with excellence even when some subsidiary element is deficient.

द्वितीयं नाम प्रस्तौति -- तदिति। तदित्युदाहृत्येति पूर्वस्यानुषङ्गः। तदित्युदाहृत्य शुद्धचित्तैर्मोक्षकाङक्षिभिपुरुषैः फलाभिसंधिमकृत्वा यज्ञाद्याः क्रियाः क्रियन्ते अतश्चित्तशोधनद्वारेण फलसंकल्पत्याजनेन मुमुक्षुत्वसंपादकत्वात्तच्छब्दनिर्देशः प्रशस्त इत्यर्थः।

He introduces the second name, Tat, carrying forward ‘having uttered.’ After uttering ‘Tat,’ persons of pure mind who desire liberation perform sacrifice and the other rites without intending their fruits. Therefore the designation ‘Tat’ is praiseworthy because, by removing resolve toward fruit and purifying the mind, it produces the desire for liberation.

सच्छब्दस्य प्राशस्त्यमाह -- सद्भाव इति द्वाभ्याम्। सद्भावे अस्तित्वे देवदत्तस्य पुत्रादिकमस्तीत्यस्मिन्नर्थे? साधुभावे च साधुत्वे देवदत्तस्य पुत्रादिश्रेष्ठमित्यस्मिन्नर्थे सदित्येतत्पदं प्रयुज्यते। प्रशस्ते माङ्गलिके विवाहादिकर्मणि च सदिदं कर्मेति सच्छब्दो युज्यते प्रयुज्यते संगच्छत इति वा।

He explains the excellence of the word Sat in two verses. ‘Sat’ is used for existence, as in ‘Devadatta has a son,’ and for goodness or excellence, as in ‘Devadatta’s son is excellent.’ It is also appropriately applied to praiseworthy and auspicious actions such as marriage, in the sense ‘this is a good action.’

किंच -- यज्ञ इति। यज्ञादिषु च या स्थितिस्तात्पर्येणावस्थानं तदपि सदित्युच्यते। यस्य चेदं नामत्रयं स एव परमात्मा अर्थः फलं यस्य तत्तदर्थं कर्म पूजोपहारगृहाङ्गणपरिमार्जनोपलेपरङ्गमाङ्गलिकादिक्रियास्तत्सिद्धये यदन्यत्कर्म क्रियते उद्यानशालिक्षेत्रधनार्जनादिविषयं तत्कर्म तदर्थीयं। तच्चातिव्यवहितमपि सदित्येवाभिधीयते। यस्मादेवमतिप्रशस्तमेतन्नामत्रयं तस्मादेतत्सर्वकर्मसाद्गुण्यार्थं कीर्तयेदिति तात्पर्यार्थः। अत्र चार्थवादानुपपत्त्या विधिः कल्प्यतेविधेयं स्तूयते वस्तु इति न्यायात्। अपरे तुप्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः? क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः इत्यादि वर्तमानोपदेशःसमिधो यजति इत्यादिवद्विधितया परिणमनीय इत्याहुः। तत्तुसद्भावे साधुभावे च इत्यादिषु प्राप्तार्थत्वान्न संगच्छत इति पूर्वोक्तक्रमेण विधिकल्पनैव ज्यायसी।

Further, steadfast commitment in sacrifice and similar acts is also called Sat. Any action whose intended result is the Supreme Self designated by these three names is ‘for That’: acts such as worship, offerings, sweeping, smearing and decorating a house-courtyard with auspicious designs, as well as more remotely connected actions done to enable them, such as maintaining gardens, halls and fields or acquiring wealth, are called Sat even when their connection is indirect. Because these three names are so excellent, the purport is that they should be uttered to confer excellence on all actions. Since mere praise would otherwise be purposeless, an injunction is inferred according to the principle that a prescribed object is praised. Others hold that present-tense statements such as ‘the prescribed rites proceed’ and ‘they are performed by seekers of liberation’ themselves become injunctions like ‘he sacrifices with kindling.’ But because passages such as ‘in the sense of existence and goodness’ state facts already established, that interpretation does not fit; inferring an injunction in the way just described is preferable.

इदानीं सर्वकर्मसु श्रद्धयैव प्रवृत्त्यर्थमश्रद्धाकृतं सर्वं निन्दति -- अश्रद्धयेति। अश्रद्धया हुतं हवनं? दत्तं दानं? तप्तं निर्वर्तितं तपः। यच्चान्यदपि कृतं कर्म तत्सर्वमसदित्युच्यते। यतस्तत्प्रेत्य लोकान्तरे न फलति विगुणत्वात्। नो इह न चास्मिंल्लोके फलति? अयशस्करत्वात्।

Finally, to ensure that all actions are undertaken with faith, He condemns everything performed without faith. An oblation offered without faith, a gift given without faith, austerity practiced without faith, and any other action done without faith are all called ‘asat.’ Because defective, they bear no fruit after death in another world; nor do they bear good fruit here in this world, since they produce disrepute.
